canonical_before.title: Personalized mRNA-LNP immunotherapy for canine malignant tumors
canonical_before.center: PETcura (宝科雅) multicenter IIT
canonical_before.contacts: WeChat: petcura; project team matches eligible owners with a participating veterinarian/hospital.
canonical_before.notes: Official study page updated 2026-08-15. Exploratory multicenter IIT for canine malignant tumors using fresh tumor plus paired adjacent normal tissue for >=50G RNA sequencing, neoantigen selection and personalized mRNA-LNP immunotherapy. T-cell lymphoma and brain tumors are explicitly excluded and therefore are not mapped to this record. Requires histologic or cytologic confirmation, age >=2 years, generally weight >=5 kg (smaller dogs may be individually assessed), fresh tumor and paired normal tissue obtainable at surgery; dogs already operated may still be considered if tissue was correctly frozen. Also requires adequate performance status/labs and successful LNP tolerance testing. Excludes recent chemotherapy/radiation/high-dose corticosteroids within 2 weeks, severe infection/autoimmune disease/immunodeficiency, pregnancy/lactation, and expected survival <6 months. Owners pay some sampling/freezing/sequencing costs; personalized mRNA design/manufacture is funded by PETcura.
canonical_before.funding: 🟡 Partially funded. PETcura fully funds design and manufacture of the personalized mRNA product; owners pay part of the sampling, specimen-storage and sequencing service costs. The project provides the detailed amount during enrollment assessment.
canonical_before.special_requirement: Generally age ≥2 years and weight ≥5 kg; the project explicitly allows individual assessment of smaller dogs, so low weight alone does not automatically exclude prescreening. Requires suitable fresh or correctly frozen tumor and paired normal tissue, LNP tolerance testing, adequate organ function and expected survival ≥6 months. No T-cell lymphoma or brain tumor; recent chemo/radiation/high-dose steroids require study-team review. Enrollment is assigned through PETcura across the nine published cities; exact hospitals and owner-paid sampling/sequencing costs are supplied at assessment.

canonical_before.title: Pilot anti-STEAP1 CAR-T cell therapy for canine histiocytic sarcoma
canonical_before.center: University of Pennsylvania School of Veterinary Medicine — Atherton Laboratory / Ryan Hospital
canonical_before.status: Open to limited enrollment — confirmed by investigator on 2026-09-29; study consent under revision
canonical_before.contacts: Matthew Atherton, BVSc, PhD, DECVIM — mattath@upenn.edu; Penn Vet Ryan Hospital
canonical_before.funding: The prior consent form says the study covers protocol-specified diagnostic tests, procedures and treatments. Treatment of complications directly caused by study treatment is covered up to $1,000; the owner pays costs above that limit and care before enrollment, for disease progression or for unrelated conditions. Coverage may change in the revised consent form; confirm with Penn before enrollment.
canonical_before.special_requirement: STEAP1 expression in tumor tissue, adequate screening results and remaining pilot enrollment capacity must be confirmed by Penn; archived tumor tissue may be used for diagnosis and target screening.
canonical_before.notes: First-in-dog pilot treatment and safety/dose study: autologous T cells engineered against STEAP1 after two bendamustine preconditioning doses, followed by CAR-T infusion and repeated follow-up visits for about six months. No clinical benefit is established. Investigator email to an owner on 2026-09-29 confirms current limited enrollment and requires measurable disease; prior cancer treatment does not itself exclude enrollment, but concurrent chemotherapy must stop before participation under Penn's direction. A previously issued consent form identifies investigators Matthew Atherton and Jennifer Lenz and footer POAP735 / IACUC807805 / IBC22-287 & 25-312 (version 22 Dec 2025); the investigator says the form is being revised, so schedule, costs and remaining eligibility require fresh confirmation. This is a distinct histiocytic-sarcoma protocol from Penn's bendamustine trial for relapsed lymphoma.
canonical_before.intervention: Autologous anti-STEAP1 CAR-T cells after bendamustine preconditioning

canonical_before.title: Autologous tumour vaccine with doxorubicin after surgery for canine splenic hemangiosarcoma
canonical_before.center: University of Melbourne multicentre study — MediPaws Sydney site
canonical_before.status: Recruiting at MediPaws Sydney — participating site confirms active enrolment
canonical_before.contacts: MediPaws oncology, Dr Sonya Yu: 1800 678 387; contact via the MediPaws clinical research page
canonical_before.funding: 🟡 The autologous tumour vaccine is free. Owners pay for standard veterinary care, including doxorubicin chemotherapy and associated costs.
canonical_before.notes: University of Melbourne Animal Ethics Committee project 35274. At the verified Sydney site, dogs must have a confirmed splenic hemangiosarcoma diagnosis, completed splenectomy, no visible metastatic disease before chemotherapy and a plan to receive doxorubicin. The vaccine is prepared from the removed tumour. This is one multicentre protocol; other participating hospitals are not listed until their specific enrolment pathway is confirmed. Eligibility and tissue suitability require oncology-team assessment. Experimental vaccine efficacy is unknown.
canonical_before.intervention: Autologous tumour vaccine prepared from the resected splenic tumour, added to standard doxorubicin chemotherapy

canonical_before.title: FLASH proton radiation with or without gilvetmab for canine glioma
canonical_before.center: Penn Vet Ryan Veterinary Hospital
canonical_before.contacts: Penn Vet VCIC — 215-573-0302; vcic@vet.upenn.edu
canonical_before.funding: 🟡 Partially funded. Owners pay screening diagnostics; after enrollment the sponsor covers three FLASH-RT treatments, examinations, laboratory tests, sedation/anesthesia, CSF taps, gilvetmab infusions and protocol CT/MRI imaging.
canonical_before.notes: Dogs need histopathologic confirmation of glioma or diagnostic MRI showing a supratentorial lesion consistent with glioma, must be suitable for general anesthesia, and must have a tumor compatible with the FLASH equipment. Systemic chemotherapy or immunotherapy requires a three-week washout; prior gilvetmab is not allowed. All dogs receive three FLASH proton treatments and are randomized to receive or not receive three gilvetmab infusions, with 12 follow-up visits over 11 months.
